stack_spec.name: Built with Spec4 (BWS4)
stack_spec.description: A unified web app that showcases Spec4 through a gallery of illustrative example apps demonstrating agentic AI patterns: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool-use, a visual embeddings explorer, a single-call (simple vs. structured-output) demo, a two-step chained-calls (role-played writer/critic) demo, a plan-first planning-agent trip-day planner demo, an interleaved ReAct reason-act-observe search-loop demo presented as its deliberate counterpart, an orchestrated-subagents demo in which a coordinator picks two specialists from a fixed roster, briefs them, runs them in parallel and merges their answers, and a multi-agent collaboration demo in which a buyer agent and two rival seller agents holding sealed private constraints negotiate a competitive procurement award over A2A-shaped peer messages across a code-enforced opacity boundary.

languages.name: Python
languages.role: backend service — REST API, LiteLLM/OpenRouter orchestration, RAG pipeline, embeddings example app (embedding + PCA projection), single-call example app (simple/structured generation), chained-calls example app (two-step role-played generation via PydanticAI), planning-agent example app (planner/executor agents with tool-calling via PydanticAI, SSE streaming), ReAct loop example app (hand-rolled bounded reason-act-observe loop with per-cycle PydanticAI typed calls, direct shared Exa search calls, semantic near-duplicate query guard, SSE streaming), orchestrated-subagents example app (coordinator delegation, concurrent knowledge-only specialists via asyncio.gather, merge, SSE streaming), multi-agent collaboration example app (A2A-shaped Pydantic protocol models, shared in-process peer message bus with slice-local opacity policy, deterministic RFQ composition, concurrent seller bid rounds, buyer counter/award turns, concurrent reveal and sensitivity explanation calls, SSE streaming), shared framework services (generation, embedding, storage, usage limiting, content moderation, peer message bus), Neon/Postgres access

languages.name: TypeScript
languages.role: browser client — single-page app presenting the landing page and all example apps

targets.name: web_client
targets.purpose: the browser UI presenting the landing page and every example app (RAG, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning-agent, ReAct loop, orchestrated-subagents, multi-agent collaboration, future patterns), with per-example-app code-splitting so the gallery can grow without bloating the initial load
targets.hosting: Render Static Site (free tier — no spin-down, served via CDN)
targets.build: Vite build producing a hashed static bundle with route-based lazy-loaded chunks per example app
targets.distribution: served at the app's root domain

targets.name: api
targets.purpose: serves the SPA's data needs — LiteLLM/OpenRouter orchestration, RAG pipeline (chunking, embedding, retrieval), embeddings example app (preconfigured/custom text embedding and 2D projection), single-call example app (simple text and structured/schema-conforming generation), chained-calls example app (two-step role-played generation via PydanticAI/OpenRouter), planning-agent example app (planner call, plan validation, tool-using executor calls streamed via server-sent events), ReAct loop example app (custom-question suitability check, the bounded interleaved reason-act-observe loop with per-cycle typed model calls and direct Exa searches, run-record persistence and retrieval, hop-source annotation, all streamed via server-sent events), orchestrated-subagents example app (moderation gate, coordinator delegation decision, two concurrent knowledge-only specialists, merged answer, all streamed via server-sent events), multi-agent collaboration example app (deterministic RFQ composition, two concurrent seller bid rounds, buyer counter and award turns, concurrent reveal/sensitivity explanation calls, A2A-shaped peer messages delivered over the shared in-process bus with code-enforced opacity, NegotiationRecord persistence, all streamed via server-sent events), Exa search integration, and shared framework services (generation, embedding, storage, usage limiting, content moderation, peer message bus)
targets.runtime: Python 3.12 on a Render free Web Service (spins down after ~15 min idle; cold-starts on next request; 750 free instance-hours/month)
targets.build: container image or native Python buildpack from the repo
targets.api_contract: REST; OpenAPI schema auto-generated by FastAPI; the planning-agent run endpoint streams incremental JSON results (Plan, then StepResults, then Itinerary) as server-sent events over a POST request; the ReAct loop run endpoint streams one JSON envelope per event type (run_started, cycle_thought, cycle_action, cycle_observation, cycle_counter, final_answer, budget_exhausted, error) as server-sent events over a POST request, with the completed trace also retrievable via GET /api/react/run/{run_id}; the orchestrated-subagents run endpoint likewise streams the DelegationDecision, then per-specialist status/answer events as the concurrent specialist tasks complete, then the MergedAnswer; the multi-agent collaboration run endpoint streams one event per negotiation stage (QuotationRequest, per-seller opening bid events as the concurrent bids complete, CounterOffers, per-seller best-and-final bid events, Award, then the reveal and sensitivity panels as their concurrent explanation calls complete), all as server-sent events over a POST request

exposure.cors: allow only the web_client's own origin

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose free model for grounded, structured-output answers (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured/tool-oriented output (google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free)
a capable general-purpose free model able to produce both plain text and JSON-schema-conforming structured output for a single direct prompt/response demo (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured/JSON output, for the single-call demo

OpenRouter (via LiteLLM).fallback: Gemini 2.0 Flash free takes over automatically via LiteLLM routing if the primary Llama 3.3 70B free model's rate limit is hit or it errors, for both the RAG and single-call tiers

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose free model able to sustain a distinct role-played persona (struggling writer, harsh critic) across a two-step sequential chain (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free)
a fast alternate free model, also strong at persona/role-played and structured JSON output, for the chained-calls demo

a capable free model with reliable native tool-calling and structured output, able to decompose a trip goal into a validated small plan and to execute research/synthesis steps against a web-search tool
a fast alternate free model, also capable of tool-calling and structured JSON output, for the planner and executor calls

a capable free model with reliable typed/structured output able to emit, per cycle, a short thought plus a discriminated action — either the exact search query to issue or the decision that it can now answer — reading each new observation from the loop's assembled context; no native tool-calling is required of it because the search is executed by application code between cycles
a fast alternate free model, also reliable at typed thought/action output, for any cycle of the ReAct loop or its final-answer call

a capable free model with reliable typed output producing a suitability verdict for a visitor's own question — whether it chains two or more facts, whether it needs live information, an estimated hop count and a confidence — so a single-hop or unanswerable free-form question is flagged before the loop spends its budget
a fast alternate free model with reliable typed output, for the custom-question suitability check

a capable free model with reliable typed output producing, after a run completes, the per-hop source annotation — for each fact the answer rests on, whether it came from an observation in the trace or from the model's own parametric knowledge, and which cycle supplied it — so the overview's teaching point about where observation was genuinely required is grounded in the run's own trace rather than asserted
a fast alternate free model with reliable typed output, for the post-run hop-source annotation call

a capable general-purpose free model with reliable structured output, able to (a) choose exactly two specialists from a fixed roster of four and write a distinct brief for each, (b) answer a briefed sub-question as a knowledge-only specialist with no tool access, and (c) merge two independent specialist answers into one integrated response
a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured JSON output, for the coordinator delegation call, either specialist call, or the merge call

structured-output generation of the disagreement note comparing the two specialist answers; produced as fields on the merge call's existing structured output rather than as an additional model call, so the run's three-call budget is unchanged

a capable free model with reliable structured output, able to sustain a private-constraint-bound negotiating persona across bid → counter → best-and-final turns without disclosing its sealed position, and to award a deal with a rationale weighed explicitly against the visitor's stated priority weighting

a fast alternate free model, also strong at structured JSON output and persona adherence, for any of the six negotiation turns (either seller's opening bid, the buyer's counter-offers, either seller's best-and-final bid, the buyer's award)

a capable free model with strict JSON-Schema conformance, producing the end-of-run private-position reveal explanation for each party — why a seller held firm or conceded on a given axis, read against its now-unsealed constraints; a dedicated thin-schema call rather than extra fields on the award call, so a conformance failure degrades only the reveal panel and never the award payload
a fast alternate free model with strict JSON-Schema conformance, for the private-position reveal explanation call

a capable free model with strict JSON-Schema conformance, producing the counterfactual priority-sensitivity explanation — whether a different priority weighting would have changed the winner and why; a dedicated call because asking the award turn to both decide and reason counterfactually about its own decision in one shot is an unreliable prompt
a fast alternate free model with strict JSON-Schema conformance, for the priority-sensitivity explanation call

OpenRouter (via PydanticAI).fallback: Gemini 2.0 Flash free takes over automatically via PydanticAI's native FallbackModel if the primary Llama 3.3 70B free model errors or hits its rate limit — for either step of the chained-calls chain, for any planner or executor call of the planning-agent run, for any per-cycle thought/action call, the final-answer call, the custom-question suitability check or the post-run hop-source annotation of the ReAct loop run, for the coordinator delegation call, either specialist call, or the merge call of the orchestrated-subagents run, and for any of the six negotiation turns or either of the two explanation calls of the multi-agent collaboration run; all slugs are read from the same shared ordered free-tier model chain in model_registry.py used by the LiteLLM lane, with no second capability chain introduced for the ReAct app

integrations.name: Exa Search API
integrations.purpose: fetch ranked, real external search results (title, summary/snippet, source) so tool-use example apps can incorporate outside information, serve as the model-invoked web-search tool for the planning-agent example app's research steps, and serve as the observation source for each act step of the ReAct loop example app, where the exact query the model chose is issued verbatim and its returned snippets are rendered as the cycle's observation

integrations.name: OpenAI Moderation API (omni-moderation-latest)
integrations.purpose: pre-dispatch safety classification of visitor-supplied free-form questions (abuse, self-harm, sexual, hate, violence, illicit) before any coordinator call is made; chosen because the moderation endpoint is free of charge and does not consume the OpenRouter free-model allowance, so the orchestrated-subagents run's three-model-call budget is unaffected; exposed as a shared framework service so any future example app with a free-form input can reuse it, and invoked only for free-form input — curated preset questions are pre-vetted and skip it entirely; the ReAct loop example app reuses this same shared service for its free-form visitor questions before the suitability check, and its five curated presets bypass it; the multi-agent collaboration example app has no free-text input at all (scenario enum plus a numeric weighting vector) and therefore never calls it
integrations.protocol: REST over HTTPS; POST /v1/moderations, called with httpx and parsed into a Pydantic ModerationVerdict
integrations.auth: API key; OPENAI_API_KEY (entered in the Render dashboard as a sync:false secret, as the OpenRouter and Exa keys are)

primary_store.purpose: durable relational store for everything the app writes, doubling as the vector index for the RAG example app
primary_store.durability: source of truth; survives restarts and redeploys, including Render's free-tier spin-down; Neon's free tier persists indefinitely (unlike Render's free Postgres, which expires after 30 days)

collections.name: usage_limits
physical: usage window column keyed to the current UTC hour, plus the per-UTC-day cap window
collections.purpose: the showcase-wide model/search allowance gate, enforced server-side before every provider call by every example app, windowed per UTC hour and per UTC day; the multi-agent collaboration example app's runs-per-hour limit is this existing framework-standard gate rather than a tightened per-app counter, and the ReAct loop app's every model call and every Exa search is accounted here as well, since it is the most expensive example per run

collections.name: allowance_holds
collections.purpose: reserve/redeem/refund records against the showcase-wide hourly usage gate, so a run's full call budget is held before its first model call and a confirmed dispatch either completes or is refused up front with a clear reason; the orchestrated-subagents run holds three calls before the coordinator delegation call, and the multi-agent collaboration run holds all eight (six negotiation plus two explanation) before the deterministic RFQ is composed; the ReAct loop run holds its full worst-case ceiling (up to 8 search-cycle calls plus 1 final-answer call plus the post-run annotation call) before the first cycle, and refunds the unspent remainder when the loop answers early — which is the common case, so refunding rather than charging the ceiling is what keeps the generous budget affordable; refunded when a run fails before spending its reserved calls
physical: index on capability and usage window

collections.name: moderation_log
collections.purpose: safety-gate telemetry for free-form question moderation: a salted hash of the question (never the raw text), the returned category, confidence, latency, and whether the call failed closed; satisfies the capability's privacy requirement that raw visitor question text is not retained; now also written for the ReAct loop app's free-form questions, which pass the same shared gate
physical: salted question hash column; no raw question text column

collections.name: negotiation_runs
collections.purpose: the immutable per-run negotiation record header written at run end: the selected scenario id and priority weighting, the deterministically composed QuotationRequest, both rounds of bids, the buyer's counter-offers, the award with its priority references, the reveal and sensitivity explanation payloads, per-stage timings, model_calls_used, and degradation flags for any stage that failed or returned non-conforming output; stage payloads are held as JSONB while the header columns carry the queryable telemetry the capability's eval signal needs — model_calls_used is alerted on when the negotiation-stage count differs from six
physical: negotiation_stage_call_count and total_model_calls_used columns (queryable, not buried in JSONB)
JSONB columns for the RFQ, opening bids, counter-offers, final bids, award, reveal and sensitivity payloads

collections.name: peer_messages
collections.purpose: one row per A2A-shaped peer message exchanged during a run, foreign-keyed to negotiation_runs, so the chronological sender-to-recipient message log is a stored projection rather than a client-side tally and the app's headline opacity claim is provable from the store: seller_to_seller_count is a single SQL predicate over sender and recipient, expected to be zero for every run
physical: sender and recipient columns (indexed together, so seller-to-seller traffic is queryable)
JSONB work-item column carrying the A2A-shaped Task/Message/Artifact payload

collections.name: react_runs
collections.purpose: the per-run ReAct trace record written at run end and read back whole by GET /api/react/run/{run_id}: the ordered cycles (thought, action kind, exact query issued, observation snippets or explicit empty-result flag), the terminal card (final answer with the observations it drew on, or budget-exhausted with what remained unresolved), the custom-question suitability verdict where one was made, and the post-run hop-source annotations; the eval-signal metrics the capability names are queryable header columns rather than JSONB traversal, because reading a whole trace by run_id is the only read pattern the feature has while the metrics are aggregated across runs
physical: id (primary, the run_id used by the retrieval route)

queryable header columns: question_origin (preset id or 'custom'), searches_used, cycle_budget, ending ('final_answer' | 'budget_exhausted'), duplicate_queries_blocked, empty_observations, suitability_verdict fields (chained_facts, needs_live_info, estimated_hops, confidence), annotation_outcome
JSONB ordered cycle-trace column (thought, action_kind, query_text, observation snippets, is_empty, status per cycle)

embedding_projection_cache.choice: in-process NumPy array of preconfigured embeddings + fitted PCA model, held in memory (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 vectors, scikit-learn PCA)
embedding_projection_cache.purpose: fills the vector_index substrate for the embeddings example app's custom_text_semantic_placement capability: holds the preconfigured examples' embeddings and the fitted PCA projection so a new custom-text point can be transformed into the same stable 2D layout without recomputing it, and without persisting user-entered custom text beyond the request per the capability's privacy requirement
embedding_projection_cache.durability: ephemeral — rebuilt from bundled_assets' preconfigured_text_examples at process startup or on first request; ephemeral in-process derived state, rebuildable, not a source of truth; custom text embeddings exist only for the duration of the request and are never persisted

collections.name: preconfigured_example_embeddings
physical: in-process NumPy array, 384-dim (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) per preconfigured example
fitted PCA model held in memory, reused via .transform() for custom text

react_query_guard_cache.choice: in-process NumPy array of the current run's issued-query embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via the shared sentence-transformers service), held for the lifetime of one run
react_query_guard_cache.purpose: backs the semantic near-duplicate query guard: each candidate query the model chooses is embedded and cosine-compared against the queries already issued in this run, so a rephrased repeat is blocked before it spends a search and the loop cannot burn its budget circling the same question; scoped to a single run because duplicate detection is only ever meaningful within one trace, and held in process because the shared embedding service spends no third-party quota
react_query_guard_cache.durability: ephemeral — exists only for the duration of one run and is discarded when the run ends; not a source of truth and never persisted, so a visitor's question text is not retained by the guard

collections.name: issued_query_embeddings
physical: in-process NumPy array, 384-dim (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) per query issued so far in the run
cosine-similarity comparison against a tuned duplicate threshold

bundled_assets.choice: static content bundled at build time
bundled_assets.purpose: read-only content that only changes via a code change/redeploy, not user action

collections.name: example_app_directory
collections.purpose: the single shared description of available example apps from which both the landing-page roster and the persistent hamburger navigation are drawn, so an example cannot appear in one and not the other; extended this revision with the ReAct Loop entry

collections.name: preconfigured_text_examples
collections.purpose: the curated set of words, short phrases, and sentences spanning multiple categories used to seed the embeddings example app's plot

collections.name: preset_prompts
collections.purpose: the curated set of example prompts (e.g. summarize, classify, extract) with their labeled intent, offered as one-click choices in the single-call example app

collections.name: persona_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates and few-shot exemplars defining the 'struggling writer' and 'harsh critic' personas used by the two chained calls; read-only, versioned in-repo alongside the RAG and single-call prompt conventions

collections.name: planning_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the planning-agent example app: the planner prompt (goal decomposition into a bounded, validated plan of research + synthesis steps) and the synthesis prompt (composing the final one-day itinerary from step results); read-only, versioned in-repo following the same prompt-versioning convention as the other example apps

collections.name: specialist_roster_config
collections.purpose: the fixed roster of four knowledge-only specialists (Technical, Financial, Historical, Practical) with each one's id, display name, scope description, and column colour; read as the closed set the coordinator must choose exactly two from, and used to validate the delegation decision before it is shown to the visitor

collections.name: curated_presets
collections.purpose: curated preset questions, each with a preset id and its wording, chosen so different presets produce visibly different specialist pairings; preset questions are pre-vetted and therefore bypass the moderation gate that free-form questions pass through

collections.name: orchestration_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the orchestrated-subagents example app: the coordinator delegation prompt (choose exactly two roster specialists, give a pairing rationale, write a distinct brief for each), the specialist prompt (answer only your own brief, knowledge-only, no tools), and the merge prompt (reconcile and integrate the two answers and note where they disagree); read-only, versioned in-repo following the same prompt-versioning convention as the other example apps

collections.name: procurement_scenario_catalog
collections.purpose: the pre-tuned procurement scenarios and the selectable priority weightings for the multi-agent collaboration example app: per scenario, the goods description, the buyer's baseline requirements and BATNA, and the negotiable term axes (price, delivery lead time, quantity and partial fulfilment, warranty); each scenario is hand-tuned so the sellers' sealed constraints force genuinely non-comparable bids, and each weighting preset carries its per-axis weights so the same scenario can yield a different winner; authored as version-controlled typed Python literals rather than the AI spec's suggested YAML, so mypy strict checks these deeply nested fixtures and no serialisation dependency is added — same read-only, redeploy-only-change semantics either way

collections.name: sealed_private_constraints
collections.purpose: per scenario and per seller, the hidden negotiating position — cost floor, capacity ceiling, delivery capability, warranty liability limit — plus the reveal headline and explanation seed used by the end-of-run unsealing; authored as typed Python literals in the same fixture module as the scenario they belong to, because the sealing is enforced by the message bus's opacity policy at access time (an agent can only ever load its own constraints) rather than by file separation, which would imply a boundary the filesystem is not providing

collections.name: agent_identity_cards
collections.purpose: the three A2A-shaped identity cards (buyer plus two rival sellers) published for inspection before or during a run: name, provider organisation, declared skills, declared capabilities, and explicit tool_access of none; authored as typed Python literals conforming to the slice's hand-rolled AgentCard model

collections.name: collaboration_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the multi-agent collaboration example app: the seller opening-bid and best-and-final prompts (bid within your own sealed constraints, you cannot see the rival), the buyer counter-offer prompt (target each seller on its weakest axis against the stated priorities), the buyer award prompt (choose and justify against the stated priorities), and the two thin-schema explanation prompts for the private-position reveal and the priority-sensitivity counterfactual; read-only, versioned in-repo following the same prompt-versioning convention as the other example apps

collections.name: react_preset_catalog
collections.purpose: the five curated multi-hop preset questions for the ReAct loop example app, with maintainer-authored metadata per preset: the expected hop facts, which hops require observation rather than parametric knowledge, why each hop defeats memorised knowledge (time-variable or genuinely obscure), and whether the preset is one of the three guaranteed fully-observed demonstrations; stores questions ONLY and never answers, so time-variable answers self-refresh from live search on every run and maintenance is limited to an occasional check that each question still reads sensibly; authored as typed Python literals following the collab scenario-catalog precedent, so mypy strict checks the fixtures and no serialisation dependency is added

collections.name: react_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static system-prompt templates for the ReAct loop example app: the per-cycle reason/action prompt (given the question and the observations so far, emit one short thought plus either the exact next search query or the decision to answer), the final-answer prompt (answer naming which observations it drew on), the custom-question suitability prompt, and the post-run hop-source annotation prompt; read-only, versioned in-repo following the same prompt-versioning convention as the other example apps

collections.name: educational_overviews
collections.purpose: the per-app short educational overview content — pattern explanation, quota rationale, and cross-references — including this revision's ReAct Loop overview (the loop, how it differs from a single search decision and from a fixed pre-approved plan, and the note that on the two more familiar presets the model may state an early hop from its own knowledge) and the updated Planning Agent overview cross-referencing ReAct Loop as its interleaved counterpart

browser_local_storage.purpose: keeps small per-device visitor state across visits without a backend round trip, and keeps each example app's own demonstration run counter and prior results on the device so they survive navigating away and back
browser_local_storage.durability: persists per-device/browser only; not a source of truth, not shared across devices; resettable by the visitor — hard quota protection is always the server-side usage_limits gate plus per-run call ceilings, never this store

collections.name: theme_preference
collections.purpose: the visitor's chosen light/dark theme

collections.name: run_allowance
collections.purpose: advisory per-session run counter and cap for the planning-agent example app, shown to the user with remaining runs; deliberately client-side only — hard quota protection remains the server-side usage_limits gate plus the fixed per-run call ceiling enforced by plan validation

collections.name: orchestrated_run_allowance
collections.purpose: the orchestrated-subagents example app's three-run session counter plus the visitor's own prior run records (delegation decision, per-specialist briefs, specialist answers, merged answer), stamped with the UTC hour so the counter resets on the same hourly clock as the server-side showcase-wide gate; persisting the records here is what lets the runs-remaining count and previously produced results survive navigating away and back with no server-side visitor identity at all, and hard quota protection remains the server-side usage_limits gate plus the reserved three-call budget

collections.name: last_negotiation_run
collections.purpose: a cache of the visitor's most recent multi-agent collaboration run so the negotiation record, reveal and message log rehydrate instantly on returning to the app without a server round trip; layered over the authoritative negotiation_runs/peer_messages persistence rather than replacing it, and this app has no per-app session counter here because its run limit is the framework-standard hourly usage_limits gate

collections.name: react_run_allowance
collections.purpose: the ReAct loop example app's two-run session counter — the gallery's tightest per-app limit, because this is the most expensive example per run — plus the run_id and rendered trace of the visitor's own prior runs, stamped with the UTC hour so the counter resets on the same clock as the server-side showcase-wide gate; this is what lets the runs-remaining indicator and previously produced traces stay on screen after the runs are exhausted and survive navigating away and back with no server-side visitor identity, while hard quota protection remains the server-side usage_limits gate plus the allowance_holds reservation of the run's worst-case call ceiling; the stored run_id lets the full trace be re-fetched from GET /api/react/run/{run_id} rather than trusting the cached copy

chunking_pipeline.choice: hand-rolled paragraph/fixed-window text splitter, in application code
chunking_pipeline.purpose: splits reference_dataset documents into passages before embedding; kept simple and transparent given the small curated dataset, serving the project's teaching-clarity goal

embedding_pipeline.choice: sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), in-process at index time and query time
embedding_pipeline.purpose: fills the catalog's embedding_pipeline substrate for both the RAG example (vectors written to and read from dataset_embeddings) and the embeddings example app (vectors for preconfigured examples and custom text, held in embedding_projection_cache) — the same shared embedding model is reused rather than introduced separately; this revision adds a third consumer, the ReAct loop's semantic near-duplicate query guard, which embeds each candidate query in process and spends no third-party quota, again reusing the same shared model rather than introducing a new one; the package itself is listed under libraries

retriever.choice: SQLAlchemy query using pgvector's cosine-distance operator against dataset_embeddings
retriever.purpose: finds the top-N passages most similar to a question's embedding, to ground the generated answer

pipeline_runner.choice: PydanticAI, using its OpenRouterProvider and native FallbackModel to run the fixed two-step 'struggling writer' → 'harsh critic' sequence, with the first call's response passed directly as the second call's input
pipeline_runner.purpose: fills the catalog's pipeline_runner substrate for the chained-calls example app; chosen over a hand-rolled function because upcoming example apps will coordinate multiple agents, and PydanticAI's typed Agent primitives extend naturally to that without a framework swap; the free-model slugs used by its OpenRouterProvider and FallbackModel are read from the same shared model-slug config module the LiteLLM lane uses, and the existing usage_limits/service_log_entries quota-check function gates calls on this path exactly as it gates the LiteLLM path

agent_loop_runtime.choice: PydanticAI agent runs (OpenRouterProvider + FallbackModel, slugs from the shared model-slug config) in two deliberately different control shapes: (a) for the planning-agent example app, one structured-output planner call produces a Pydantic-validated Plan capped at 2–3 executor steps (trimmed or re-planned with a note if nonconforming), then executor steps run sequentially only after the user's explicit go-ahead; (b) for the ReAct loop example app, a hand-rolled bounded while-loop in backend/app/react/ owns the iteration — each cycle is one PydanticAI call returning a validated ReactStep (short thought plus a discriminated action, either search(query) or answer), the slice executes the search between cycles, appends the observation to the assembled context, advances the cycle counter, and terminates on either the model's answer decision or the ~8-search ceiling; in both shapes the shared usage-limit gate is checked before every model call and each result is streamed to the client as it completes
agent_loop_runtime.purpose: fills the catalog's agent_loop_runtime substrate for the planning-agent example app and, this revision, for the ReAct loop example app; the ReAct loop is hand-rolled rather than delegated to PydanticAI's native tool-calling iteration for three reasons the feature depends on: the cycle count must be a code invariant so allowance_holds can reserve a known worst-case budget up front, every cycle boundary must be a first-class SSE emission point so thought, action and observation are separately visible rather than buried in framework message history, and the near-duplicate query guard must run between the model's chosen query and the search being issued; a readable loop is also the lesson itself in an app whose purpose is to make the loop visible, following the same teaching-clarity precedent as the hand-rolled chunking pipeline and message bus, and keeping the project on one agent framework; the PydanticAI package itself is listed under libraries

tool_execution_harness.choice: two fillings of the same substrate, per app: (a) for the planning-agent example app, PydanticAI native tool-calling (tool registration on the executor agent) wrapping the existing Exa search client (httpx) as a typed web-search tool for research steps; (b) for the ReAct loop example app, a direct in-process call from the loop's act step to the shared Exa wrapper at backend/app/services/web_search.py — no tool registration, no MCP — with the semantic near-duplicate guard interposed before the call and the verbatim result snippets returned as the cycle's observation
tool_execution_harness.purpose: fills the catalog's tool_execution_harness substrate for the planning-agent example app and, this revision, for the ReAct loop example app, following the spec's tool protocol strategy in each case: the ReAct act step reuses the existing shared Exa wrapper as a direct in-process call and is explicitly NOT wrapped in MCP; the direct-call shape is what lets application code hold the search budget, interpose the duplicate guard, and render the exact query issued alongside its snippets so the trace is honest; in both apps the run-allowance/quota check is a direct internal service-layer call, never a model-exposed tool, so the model cannot decide whether quota is spent; the PydanticAI and httpx packages themselves are listed under libraries

subagent_orchestration_runtime.choice: PydanticAI agents dispatched directly in-process and fanned out with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True): one structured-output coordinator agent returns a Pydantic-validated DelegationDecision (exactly two specialist ids from the fixed four-name roster, a pairing rationale, and a distinct brief per specialist, re-requested once when validation fails), then after the visitor's explicit dispatch confirmation the two knowledge-only specialist agents run as concurrent async tasks, then the coordinator agent is called a third time to merge their answers
subagent_orchestration_runtime.purpose: fills the catalog's subagent_orchestration_runtime substrate for the orchestrated-subagents example app; chosen over PydanticAI agent delegation (specialists as coordinator tools) because a model-driven tool loop could not guarantee exactly three calls and would serialise the specialists, defeating the visible parallelism the demo teaches, and because the spec requires specialists to have no tool access — the tool protocol strategy specifies a DIRECT in-process call, one async task per selected specialist, gathered via the parallel_fanout mechanism; chosen over LangGraph to avoid a second agent framework and its state-graph/checkpointing machinery on Render's free tier; gathering with return_exceptions=True is what lets one specialist fail while the other column's answer stays on screen and the merge proceeds with a note about the missing contribution; the shared usage-limit gate is checked and the full three-call budget reserved before the coordinator call, and the PydanticAI package itself is listed under libraries

agent_message_bus.choice: hand-rolled in-process message bus promoted to a shared framework service at backend/app/services/message_bus.py — an append-only ordered envelope store with deliver(message), context_for(agent_id) filtering strictly on recipient equality, and a chronological log projection — with a slice-local opacity policy layer in the collaboration app applying the buyer/seller roles, sealed-constraint access rules and the no-seller-to-seller invariant on top of it
agent_message_bus.purpose: fills the catalog's agent_message_bus substrate for the multi-agent collaboration example app, delivering each PeerMessage and assembling every agent turn's context from only the messages addressed to that agent, so peer opacity is enforced structurally in code rather than by prompt instruction — an agent's prompt cannot be built from the rival's messages because the assembly function is never given them, and this holds even when a seller reasons its way toward asking about the rival; chosen hand-rolled over a pub/sub library because subscription-by-convention would weaken the guarantee from structurally impossible to merely unsubscribed, and made a shared service (rather than slice-local) so future peer-agent examples can reuse the generic substrate while the scenario-specific rules stay in the slice; injected via FastAPI Depends like the moderation service so tests can substitute it, and unit-tested at both levels — that context_for never returns a non-addressed envelope, and that MessageLog.seller_to_seller_count is zero across every preset

protocol_runtime.choice: hand-rolled A2A-shaped Pydantic models in the collaboration slice (backend/app/collab/protocol.py): AgentCard with AgentProvider/AgentSkill/AgentCapabilities, Task with TaskStatus/TaskState, Message with Role and Part/DataPart, and Artifact — serialised camelCase per the A2A spec's convention, carried over the shared in-process message bus with no HTTP, JSON-RPC or gRPC transport binding
protocol_runtime.purpose: fills the catalog's protocol_runtime substrate for the multi-agent collaboration example app: implements A2A's Layer 1 canonical data model and Layer 2 interaction pattern while deliberately omitting Layer 3 transport bindings, exactly as the vision constrains; chosen hand-rolled over the official a2a-sdk to add no backend dependency and no cold-start import weight on Render's free tier (where spin-down makes cold start a routine path), and because a single readable models file suits a repo people read to learn — following the same teaching-clarity precedent as the hand-rolled chunking pipeline; the honesty cost is accepted and paid for in the overview, which says the exchanges are modelled on A2A's data model and interaction pattern rather than claiming the protocol's own objects, and states what a real cross-owner deployment would add (a Layer 3 transport binding, agent discovery over /.well-known/agent-card.json, and real authentication between owners)

ai_conventions.prompt_versioning: the rag_example_app's prompt template (including its structured-output schema/instructions) is stored as a versioned file in-repo (e.g. backend/app/rag/prompts/answer_v1.md), tagged with a semantic version in the filename/header, and loaded by a thin resolver function; the single_call_example_app's preset prompts follow the same convention — plain text/intent metadata stored in-repo (e.g. backend/app/single_call/prompts/presets.py or a versioned data file), with any structured-mode JSON schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models; the chained_calls_example_app's 'struggling writer' and 'harsh critic' persona system-prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/chained_calls/prompts/ (e.g. writer_v1.md, critic_v1.md), loaded by the same thin resolver pattern; the planning_agent_example_app's planner and synthesis prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/planning/prompts/ (e.g. planner_v1.md, synthesis_v1.md), with the Plan/StepResult/Itinerary structured-output schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models; the orchestrated_subagents_example_app's coordinator delegation, specialist, and merge prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/orchestrated/prompts/ (e.g. delegation_v1.md, specialist_v1.md, merge_v1.md), with the DelegationDecision/Brief/SubagentResult/MergedAnswer structured-output schemas (the merged answer carrying the disagreement note as fields on the same schema) defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models; the multi_agent_collaboration_example_app's negotiation prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/collab/prompts/ (seller_bid_v1.md, seller_final_v1.md, buyer_counter_v1.md, buyer_award_v1.md, reveal_explanation_v1.md, sensitivity_v1.md), with the Bid/CounterOffer/Award and the two thin explanation schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models, deliberately kept as separate narrow schemas per call rather than one wide award schema so that a non-conforming response degrades only its own panel; the react_loop_example_app's prompt templates follow the identical convention — versioned files under backend/app/react/prompts/ (cycle_v1.md for the per-cycle thought/action prompt, final_answer_v1.md, suitability_v1.md, hop_annotation_v1.md), with the ReactStep (thought plus discriminated search/answer action), FinalAnswer, SuitabilityVerdict and HopAnnotation schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models, each kept narrow so a conformance failure degrades only its own panel and never the trace already on screen; no external prompt-management tool

libraries.name: FastAPI

libraries.name: SQLAlchemy
libraries.purpose: ORM/toolkit for Neon Postgres access, including pgvector column types and the JSONB stage payloads of the negotiation run record and the JSONB cycle trace of the ReAct run record

libraries.name: asyncpg
libraries.purpose: async PostgreSQL driver used by SQLAlchemy's async engine to connect to Neon

libraries.name: Alembic
libraries.purpose: versioned schema migrations for the Postgres/Neon schema, including the revision adding the negotiation_runs and peer_messages tables for the multi-agent collaboration run record and its verifiable message log, and this revision's single new migration adding the react_runs table

libraries.name: httpx
libraries.purpose: async HTTP client for calling the Exa Search API without blocking the event loop (tool-use example app, the planning-agent example app's web-search tool, and the ReAct loop example app's per-cycle direct search calls through the same shared wrapper), and for the shared moderation service's POST to the OpenAI Moderation endpoint, following the same thin-client pattern as the Exa client

libraries.name: Pydantic
libraries.purpose: request/response validation, structured-output schema for the RAG answer format, per-preset schema models for the single-call example app's Structured mode, the Plan/PlanStep/StepResult/Itinerary schemas bounding the planning-agent run, the DelegationDecision/Brief/SubagentResult/MergedAnswer schemas for the orchestrated run, the ModerationVerdict model, the ReactStep/FinalAnswer/SuitabilityVerdict/HopAnnotation schemas and the typed multi-hop preset fixtures for the ReAct loop app, and — for the multi-agent collaboration app — the hand-rolled A2A-shaped protocol models (AgentCard, Task, Message, Part, Artifact), the Bid/CounterOffer/Award negotiation schemas, the two thin explanation schemas, and the typed scenario/sealed-constraint/identity-card fixture literals that mypy strict checks

libraries.name: LiteLLM
libraries.purpose: unified interface to OpenRouter's free models for text generation, with built-in retry/fallback across the primary and fallback model, used by RAG and by the single-call example app's simple and structured-output requests; its model_registry.py ordered free-tier chain remains the single shared chain that the PydanticAI lane reads too, including for this revision's ReAct capabilities

libraries.name: PydanticAI
libraries.purpose: agent framework running the chained-calls example app's fixed two-step writer→critic sequence, the planning-agent example app's planner/executor agents (structured-output planner, native tool-calling executors wrapping the Exa search tool), the orchestrated-subagents example app's coordinator and two knowledge-only specialist agents, the multi-agent collaboration example app's buyer and two seller peer agents (six schema-constrained negotiation turns plus the two post-award explanation calls, all knowledge-only with no tool access), and — this revision — the ReAct loop example app's per-cycle typed thought/action calls, its final-answer call, its custom-question suitability check and its post-run hop-source annotation, all returning validated Pydantic models so no JSON is parsed out of prose; all via its OpenRouterProvider and native FallbackModel over the one shared model chain, with the ReAct loop's iteration owned by application code rather than the framework so the call budget stays a code invariant

libraries.name: sse-starlette
libraries.purpose: server-sent events response support for FastAPI, streaming the planning-agent run's incremental results, the orchestrated-subagents run's three phases, the multi-agent collaboration run's eight stages, and the ReAct loop run's per-cycle envelopes (run_started, cycle_thought, cycle_action, cycle_observation, cycle_counter, then final_answer or budget_exhausted, or error), with built-in ping/keep-alive (important behind Render's proxy) and client-disconnect detection so an abandoned run stops spending model quota — which matters most for the ReAct loop, the gallery's most expensive example per run

libraries.name: tenacity
libraries.purpose: bounded retry with backoff around outbound calls, including the shared moderation service's call to the OpenAI moderation endpoint before it fails closed

libraries.name: sentence-transformers
libraries.purpose: in-process local embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) for text representation at index and query time, shared by the RAG pipeline, the embeddings example app, and — this revision — the ReAct loop's semantic near-duplicate query guard, so all three use the same embedding representation and no new embedding model is introduced; spends no third-party quota, which is why the guard can embed every candidate query freely

libraries.name: scikit-learn
libraries.purpose: PCA dimensionality reduction, fitted once on the preconfigured examples' embeddings and reused via .transform() for custom text, so the 2D layout stays stable across recalculations rather than jumping when a new point is added

libraries.name: numpy
libraries.purpose: numeric array support underpinning the embedding and PCA projection maths, the in-process projection cache, and the ReAct loop's per-run cosine-similarity comparison of candidate queries against those already issued

libraries.name: pgvector
libraries.purpose: Python/SQLAlchemy client for the pgvector Postgres extension, enabling vector columns and similarity queries

libraries.name: pydantic-settings
libraries.purpose: typed, validated configuration objects reading env vars/.env files (OpenRouter, Exa and OpenAI moderation keys, DB URL, CORS origin, Sentry DSN), including the ReAct loop's cycle budget and duplicate-similarity threshold

libraries.name: structlog
libraries.purpose: structured JSON logging for application events and service-log entries, including per-run orchestration telemetry, the multi-agent collaboration run's telemetry, and the ReAct loop's per-run metrics (cycles used vs budget, searches issued, duplicate queries blocked, empty observations, ending distribution, suitability verdicts on custom questions, and annotation success/retry rates)

libraries.name: sentry-sdk
libraries.purpose: backend error tracking and aggregation across FastAPI, LiteLLM, PydanticAI, Exa and moderation calls, with model-call performance spans (token usage, latency, error rates) on the free tier, including a span per ReAct cycle covering its model call and its Exa call

project_structure.purpose: thin FastAPI routers, one module per feature (landing, RAG, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning-agent, ReAct loop, orchestrated-subagents, multi-agent collaboration, shared services, health)

thin SSE router for the multi-agent collaboration run: validates the scenario enum and priority weighting, delegates to the slice service, and streams one event per negotiation stage plus the two explanation panels

thin router for the ReAct loop example app: POST run streaming the per-cycle SSE envelopes (opening its own DB session inside the generator, never via Depends, per the established streaming-route rule), GET run/{run_id} returning the persisted trace, and GET presets returning the five curated questions with their display metadata but never any stored answers

shared framework services: LLM access (LiteLLM wrapper), embedding (sentence-transformers wrapper), Exa web search, storage abstraction, shared model-slug config/model registry, and the usage-limit quota-check/logging function with reserve/redeem/refund holds — reused by both the LiteLLM and PydanticAI call paths and by the ReAct loop's direct search calls

shared content-moderation service: a generic moderate(text, calling_context) -> ModerationVerdict function calling the OpenAI moderation endpoint over httpx with tenacity-bounded retry, failing closed with a plain-language visitor message, logging only a salted hash of the input, and injected via FastAPI Depends so any example app with a free-form input can reuse it — now including the ReAct loop's custom questions

shared in-process peer message bus: append-only ordered envelope store with deliver(message), context_for(agent_id) filtering strictly on recipient equality, and a chronological log projection; generic substrate only — role and visibility policy belongs to the calling slice — and injected via FastAPI Depends so tests can substitute it
RAG-specific logic: chunking pipeline, retriever, versioned prompt templates
embeddings example app logic: bundled preconfigured TextSample set, in-process embedding + PCA fit/transform, and the API route accepting custom text and returning the recalculated 2D projection

single-call example app logic: bundled preset prompt set, per-preset Pydantic schema models for Structured mode, and the API route returning a plain-text or structured (request+response) result via the shared LiteLLM generation service
chained-calls example app logic: PydanticAI agent setup, the two-step writer→critic run function, and the API route returning the intermediate and final outputs
versioned persona system-prompt templates ('struggling writer', 'harsh critic') following the project's in-repo prompt-versioning convention

planning-agent example app logic: PydanticAI planner agent (structured-output Plan, validated and trimmed to the 2–3 step cap), Exa web-search tool registration for executor agents, the sequential user-advanced executor run function gated by the shared quota check, and the SSE route streaming Plan, StepResults, and the final Itinerary
versioned planner and synthesis prompt templates with the Plan/StepResult/Itinerary structured-output Pydantic schemas alongside

ReAct loop example app logic: the typed multi-hop preset catalog (questions and hop metadata only, never answers), the moderation gate and PydanticAI suitability check for custom questions, the hand-rolled bounded reason-act-observe loop owning the cycle counter and the ~8-search ceiling, the per-cycle PydanticAI typed thought/action call, the direct calls to the shared Exa wrapper with verbatim snippets returned as observations, the worst-case allowance_holds reservation taken before the first cycle and refunded on early answer, the terminal-card selection (final answer naming its observations, or budget-exhausted naming what remained unresolved), the post-run hop-source annotation call, the react_runs record persistence, and the per-cycle SSE emission

the semantic near-duplicate query guard: embeds each candidate query via the shared sentence-transformers service, cosine-compares it against the run's already-issued query embeddings held in an in-process NumPy array, and blocks a rephrased repeat before it spends a search; a pure function over (candidate, prior embeddings, threshold) so it is unit-testable without a model call path

versioned ReAct prompt templates (cycle_v1.md, final_answer_v1.md, suitability_v1.md, hop_annotation_v1.md) with the ReactStep/FinalAnswer/SuitabilityVerdict/HopAnnotation structured-output Pydantic schemas alongside

orchestrated-subagents example app logic: the bundled four-specialist roster config and curated preset questions, the moderation gate call for free-form questions only, the PydanticAI coordinator agent producing a validated DelegationDecision, the asyncio.gather fan-out running the two knowledge-only specialist agents concurrently with return_exceptions=True, the merge call producing the MergedAnswer with its disagreement note, the three-call budget reservation against the shared hourly usage gate, and the SSE route streaming the delegation decision, per-specialist status/answers, and the merged answer
versioned coordinator delegation, specialist, and merge prompt templates with the DelegationDecision/Brief/SubagentResult/MergedAnswer structured-output Pydantic schemas alongside

multi-agent collaboration example app logic: the opacity policy layer over the shared message bus (buyer/seller roles, own-constraints-only access, the no-seller-to-seller invariant), the deterministic RFQ composer that takes no model call, the buyer and two seller PydanticAI peer agents, the asyncio.gather concurrent bid rounds with return_exceptions=True, the buyer counter-offer and award turns, the two concurrent post-award explanation calls, the eight-call budget reservation taken against the shared hourly usage gate before the RFQ is composed, and the NegotiationRecord persistence plus per-stage SSE emission

the hand-rolled A2A-shaped Pydantic protocol models — AgentCard with AgentProvider/AgentSkill/AgentCapabilities, Task with TaskStatus/TaskState, Message with Role and Part/DataPart, and Artifact — serialised camelCase per the A2A convention, in one readable file so a visitor can see exactly what the protocol treatment does and does not include

typed Python literal fixtures, mypy-checked: the pre-tuned procurement scenario catalog, each scenario's per-seller sealed private constraints with their reveal headlines, the selectable priority-weighting presets, and the three A2A-shaped agent identity cards

versioned negotiation prompt templates (seller_bid_v1.md, seller_final_v1.md, buyer_counter_v1.md, buyer_award_v1.md, reveal_explanation_v1.md, sensitivity_v1.md) with the Bid/CounterOffer/Award and the two narrow explanation Pydantic schemas alongside
SQLAlchemy models, session factory, Alembic migrations (including the revisions adding negotiation_runs, peer_messages, and this revision's react_runs)
configuration (pydantic-settings), logging/Sentry setup

pytest suites mirroring the package layout, including message-bus tests that context_for never returns a non-addressed envelope, collaboration-slice tests that seller_to_seller_count is zero across every preset scenario and that the negotiation-stage call count is exactly six, and ReAct-slice tests that the loop never exceeds its search ceiling, that a budget-exhausted run yields the budget-exhausted card rather than an answer, that the duplicate guard blocks a rephrased query while allowing a genuine follow-up, that an empty Exa result is recorded as an explicit empty observation rather than dropped, that the preset catalog stores no answers, and that an early answer refunds the unspent reserved calls

one folder per screen: landing, RAG example, tool-use example, embeddings example, single-call example, chained-calls example, planning-agent example, ReAct loop example, orchestrated-subagents example, multi-agent collaboration example, framework console
one folder per example app (rag, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning, react, orchestrated, collab, and future additions), each lazy-loaded via its own route
the embeddings example app's route module: plot component (react-plotly.js), custom-text input, and the educational explanation of the embedding pattern

the single-call example app's route module: prompt input and preset selector, Simple/Structured mode toggle, plain-text response view, side-by-side structured request/response JSON view, and the educational explanation of the single-call pattern

the chained-calls example app's route module: initial-request input, upfront description of each call's role, labeled intermediate-output and final-output blocks, the two-call quota-conservation notice, and the educational explanation of the chained-calls pattern

the planning-agent example app's route module: city/interests input, plan display, the explicit 'Next' advance button, progressively appearing step results consumed from the SSE stream, the final itinerary view, the localStorage-backed run-allowance display, the per-run and per-session limit notices, and the educational explanation of the planning-agent pattern — updated this revision to cross-reference the ReAct Loop example as the interleaved counterpart to this app's plan-first approach

the ReAct loop example app's route module: the educational overview (the loop, how it differs from a single search decision and from a fixed pre-approved plan, and the note about presets where an early hop may come from the model's own knowledge), the five-preset selector and free-form question input with its third-party-disclosure notice and moderation/suitability messages, the start control with no plan display and no mid-run approval, the progressively filled cycle trace consuming the SSE envelopes (thought, then the exact query issued or the answer decision, then the verbatim observation snippets or an explicit empty result), the live 'search N of 8' cycle counter, the runs-remaining indicator, the two terminal cards (final answer naming its observations, or budget-exhausted naming what remained unresolved), the hop-source annotation panel, and the exhausted state that disables input and the start control with a message distinguishing this app's two-run session limit from the shared framework cap while leaving previous results on screen

the orchestrated-subagents example app's route module: preset selector and free-form question input with the moderation refusal message, the delegation-decision panel, the explicit 'Next' dispatch button, two parallel specialist columns with live independent status, the merged answer and disagreement note, the visible runs-remaining counter, the disabled-input state distinguishing the session limit from the showcase-wide allowance, and the educational explanation of the pattern

the multi-agent collaboration example app's route module: preset scenario selector and priority-weighting control (no free-text input), inspectable agent identity cards, the buyer track carrying the RFQ, counter-offers and award, two parallel seller columns with live per-seller status matching the orchestrated app's treatment, the end-of-run private-position reveal panel, the priority-sensitivity panel, the toggleable raw message-log table, the stated 8-call cost split as 6 negotiation plus 2 explanation calls, and the educational overview contrasting this pattern with orchestrated subagents and carrying the candid notes that the protocol treatment omits the network transport and that all three agents ship under one owner with the trust boundary staged for teaching

the raw message-log view: a hand-rolled Tailwind-styled table with one row per envelope (sequence, time, sender → recipient, stage, summary) and expandable plain pretty-printed JSON work items, deliberately dense and chronological so the absence of any seller-to-seller row is visible at a glance; no JSON-viewer or syntax-highlighting dependency and no copy-to-clipboard
shared UI: nav bar, theme toggle, layout shell, and the shared markdown renderer wrapper around react-markdown with its Tailwind typography styles
typed API client and TanStack Query hooks calling the backend, plus the SSE consumption hooks for the planning-agent, ReAct loop, orchestrated-subagents and multi-agent collaboration run streams
route configuration with lazy (React.lazy) imports per example app, extended this revision with the ReAct Loop route

Vitest + React Testing Library suites, including ReAct-app tests that the trace renders cycles in arrival order, that the cycle counter advances, that the budget-exhausted card is visually distinct from the final-answer card, and that exhausting the two-run allowance disables input while leaving previous traces on screen

patterns: functional core / imperative shell — pure functions for chunking/retrieval/scoring logic, PCA fit/transform, single-call schema validation, the chained-calls writer→critic sequencing, the planning-agent plan validation/trimming and step sequencing, the orchestrated-subagents delegation validation, the moderation-response mapping, the ReAct loop's duplicate-query guard, cycle-context assembly and terminal-card selection, and the collaboration app's deterministic RFQ composition, message-bus recipient filtering, opacity policy checks and award-versus-priorities consistency checks, with thin FastAPI route handlers as the imperative shell

dependency injection for shared services (LiteLLM client, PydanticAI agents, DB session, Exa client, embedding service, moderation service, peer message bus) via FastAPI's Depends, so tests can substitute them through app.dependency_overrides

concurrent agent work is dispatched in application code with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) rather than delegated to a model-driven tool loop, so call counts stay fixed and one worker's failure never cancels the other — used for the orchestrated specialist pair, the collaboration app's two seller bid rounds, and its two post-award explanation calls

iterative agent loops are likewise owned by application code, not by a framework's tool-calling iteration: the ReAct loop's cycle counter, search ceiling, duplicate guard and termination condition all live in the slice, so the call budget is a code invariant the allowance reservation can rely on, every cycle boundary is an emission point, and the loop stays readable as the lesson it exists to teach

peer visibility is enforced structurally, never by prompt instruction: an agent's turn context is assembled only from envelopes the message bus returns for that agent, so a rival's messages and sealed constraints are unreachable by construction rather than by asking the model not to look
streaming routes open their own DB session inside the async generator via async_session_factory and never take a Depends(get_db_session), because the SSE response outlives the request handler
React: function components and hooks only, no class components
custom hooks for shared frontend logic (e.g. useExampleApps, useTheme, useRunAllowance)
documentation: Google-style docstrings on every public Python function
JSDoc on every exported TypeScript function
every source file, Python and TypeScript, opens with the header comment 'Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai'

additional_decisions.name: collaboration_run_call_budget
additional_decisions.description: The declared per-run model-call budget for the multi-agent collaboration example app, and how it is disclosed and policed.
additional_decisions.value: 8 calls per run, disclosed on the page as 6 negotiation calls (2 opening bids, 1 buyer counter, 2 best-and-final bids, 1 award) plus 2 post-award explanation calls (private-position reveal, priority sensitivity); all 8 reserved via allowance_holds before the deterministic RFQ is composed so a run is never begun that cannot complete; telemetry alerts on the negotiation-stage count differing from 6, which remains the number the pattern claim rests on. This supersedes the vision's and feature spec's 'exactly 6 model calls per run' wording, which should be updated on the next vision pass.

additional_decisions.name: react_run_call_budget
additional_decisions.description: The declared per-run model-call budget for the ReAct loop example app, and how it is reserved, disclosed and released.
additional_decisions.value: Worst case 10 calls per run, disclosed on the page as up to 8 search-cycle calls plus 1 final-answer call plus 1 post-run hop-source annotation call; the full worst case is reserved via allowance_holds before the first cycle so a run is never begun that cannot complete, and the unspent remainder is refunded when the loop answers early — the common case, which is what makes the deliberately generous 8-search budget affordable. The custom-question suitability check is 1 further call charged only on free-form input, never on a preset. Telemetry records cycles used against budget so the ending distribution can be watched and a rise in budget-exhausted endings investigated.

additional_decisions.name: nfr_id_renaming_note
additional_decisions.description: Why satisfies_nfr ids differ between entries carried forward from earlier revisions and entries added in this one.
additional_decisions.value: This revision's feature specifications renumbered the project-wide non-functional goal ids. Entries added or materially changed this revision are tagged with the current ids; entries carried forward untouched retain the ids the previous implemented plan was built against, and were deliberately not re-tagged, since re-deciding settled entries is outside this revision's scope. A future revision that touches those entries should migrate their ids at that point.
